title: A smoke alarm inside the model
allegory: Projection monitoring is like a smoke alarm: it ignores everything in the air except one ingredient, measures how much of it is there, and trips before any flames show.
map: the air in the room, moment by moment
the residual-stream activation x at each token
smoke, the one thing the alarm sniffs for
the persona vector: mean(trait-on) − mean(trait-off), normalised to v̂
the smoke reading, and the line where it beeps
the projection x·v̂, compared with a threshold τ
the trait showing up in the generated text
an alarm tuned on shower steam
a vector from unfiltered pairs, tracking prompt style instead of the trait
credit: Dot product as the length of a shadow: framing borrowed from 3Blue1Brown, Essence of Linear Algebra, 'Dot products and duality'.

chapters.name: Too late to read
chapters.note: caught it ... right after it said it

cap.1: You catch a model flattering someone only after it has said it. Could you see it coming from inside, before the words come out?
cap.2: A judge grading the output works, but only once the text exists. The trait is also present in the activations, which exist while the words are still being formed.
cap.3: Output-level monitors (autoraters, keyword filters) are post hoc. A persona vector gives a cheap internal readout from the residual stream during the forward pass, before sampling.

cap.1: A smoke alarm ignores everything in the air except smoke. It beeps on rising smoke, before any flames show. This is that alarm, inside the model.
cap.2: Pick the trait's direction: its persona vector. At every token, measure how far the activation points along it. A rising reading warns you before the trait shows in the text.
cap.3: Projection-based monitoring: s = x·v̂ at a chosen layer, with no intervention in the forward pass. It is a linear readout, like a probe whose weights come from a contrastive mean difference.

cap.1: Shine a light and the activation casts a shadow along the trait's direction. The shadow's length is the reading. Past the line τ, the alarm beeps.
cap.2: A dot product with a unit vector is the length of x's shadow on that line. Normalise v first, or the reading scales with the vector's size rather than the trait.
cap.3: v = mean(pos) − mean(neg) over response tokens, v̂ = v/‖v‖. s = x·v̂ is one scalar per token and layer; pick τ from held-out trait-on and trait-off projections.

cap.1: Test the alarm before trusting it. Answers the model was told to make flattering should read high, answers told not to should read low, with little overlap.
cap.2: Project held-out responses from both prompt conditions onto the normalised vector. Clean separation is your evidence the vector tracks the trait. Heavy overlap: the alarm can't tell them apart.
cap.3: Compare baseline, positive-prompted and steered conditions against v̂ at the steering layer. Separation of the positive and negative distributions supports trait over condition.

cap.1: An alarm tuned on shower steam goes off every morning. A trait vector built from answers that never showed the trait learns the prompt's style instead.
cap.2: If many 'be sycophantic' prompts failed, the mean difference is mostly prompt style. Keep only pairs a judge confirms, and average over response tokens, not prompt tokens.
cap.3: Prompt-token activations differ by construction, whatever the model then does. response_avg_diff over judge-filtered pairs is the variant the paper finds works; unembed v to sanity-check.

chapters.name: What it can't tell

left.title: What a reading tells you
lines: the trait is present, right now
cheap: one dot product per token

right.title: What it can't tell you
lines: anything, if the vector is steam

chapters.verdict: A reading is evidence, not proof: steer to test cause.

cap.1: The alarm tells you smoke is here. It can't tell you the smoke is doing anything, or whether the flattery alarm also sniffs out made-up facts.
cap.2: Current method: one vector per trait, projected and thresholded. Still open: are sycophancy, hallucination and evil separate directions or one thing in three hats? Check cosines; steer to test cause.
cap.3: Projection is correlational; steering over a coefficient sweep gives the causal check projection alone cannot. The cosine matrix between trait vectors at a common layer is where independence gets tested.

chapters.name: One vector, three jobs
items: Watch a trait live in deployment
Flag training data that would induce the trait

cap.1: One direction, three jobs: watch a trait live, predict when finetuning will shift it, and flag risky training data. Reading comes before steering.
cap.2: The same persona vector monitors a trait in deployment, predicts and controls personality shifts from finetuning, and flags training data likely to induce the trait before you train on it.
cap.3: Monitoring is the read side of the steering toolkit: the vector you project onto is the one you steer with. Understanding and steering AI starts with a readout you have validated.

params.label: gap between trait-on and trait-off readings

caption.1: Slide the alarm line. Then shrink the gap between honest and flattering readings, as a steam-tuned vector would, and watch every line start to fail.
caption.2: With a big gap, one threshold catches nearly all flattery with few false alarms. Shrink the gap and you can only trade missed flattery for false alarms. A well-extracted vector buys the gap.
caption.3: Toy: unit-variance Gaussian projections with separation d, Φ via the logistic approximation. The catch versus false-alarm tradeoff is set by d/σ, which extraction quality moves and τ cannot.

where_else: Linear probes: a trained direction instead of a mean difference, read the same way
Flagging training data likely to induce a trait, before you train on it
Predicting personality shifts that finetuning will cause
Smoke alarms, spam scores, credit checks: many signals, one number, one line to cross

hamming.what: Reading how strongly a trait is present inside the model by measuring how far each live activation points along that trait's persona vector.
hamming.when: When you want a cheap, always-on warning for a named trait during deployment or finetuning, without waiting for a judge to read the text.
hamming.why: It watches the trait form in the activations, so you can flag or steer before the behaviour reaches the text.

object.title: The alarm sheet
object.subtitle: Answers as dots in activation space: two clouds, the arrow between their centres, and a flat alarm sheet across it.

cap.1: Every dot is one answer, as the model's insides saw it. Honest answers gather on one side, flattering answers on the other.
cap.2: Each point is a response's mean activation at one layer. The two clouds are the trait-off and trait-on conditions after judge filtering.
cap.3: Response-token mean activations at the steering layer, for held-out positive and negative conditions. Positions here are illustrative.

cap.1: The violet arrow runs from the middle of one cloud to the middle of the other. That arrow is the persona vector: nothing more than a difference of two averages.
cap.2: v = mean(trait-on) − mean(trait-off). The arrow literally joins the two cluster centres.
cap.3: The difference of class means: the direction a contrastive extraction returns, one per layer as a [n_layers, d_model] tensor.

cap.1: The alarm is a flat sheet across the arrow. Which side of the sheet a dot lands on is the whole verdict.
cap.2: Thresholding x·v̂ at τ is a flat sheet perpendicular to v. Everything on the far side trips the alarm.
cap.3: {x : x·v̂ = τ} is a hyperplane with normal v̂: monitoring is a linear classifier with a mean-difference weight vector.

cap.1: Only distance along the arrow counts. Slide a dot sideways, parallel to the sheet, and the reading does not move at all.
cap.2: Moves perpendicular to v̂ cast no shadow on it, so they leave the reading unchanged. Only the component along v̂ matters.
cap.3: s = x·v̂ is invariant to any displacement in v̂'s orthogonal complement: the monitor sees one dimension out of d_model.

cap.1: Add the arrow to an answer's insides and the dot jumps further along: that is steering. The alarm only reads where the dots already are.
cap.2: The steered cloud sits further along v, because adding α·v at that layer raises x·v̂ there by α‖v‖. Monitoring never moves a dot.
cap.3: Same vector, two verbs: read (s = x·v̂, no intervention) and write (x ← x + αv). Writing is also the causal check reading cannot supply.

predict.q: You nudge an activation sideways, parallel to the alarm sheet. What happens to the reading?

options.t: Nothing: only the part along the vector counts

predict.why: A dot product with a unit vector keeps only the shadow on that line. Sideways moves cast no shadow.

predict.q: Your alarm fires on every answer whose system prompt asked for flattery, whether or not the answer flatters. The likely cause?

options.t: The vector learned prompt style: unfiltered pairs or prompt-token averaging
The threshold is set too high

predict.why: Prompt activations differ by construction. Filter pairs with a judge and average over response tokens only.

predict.q: The reading is high. Does that prove this direction causes the flattery?

options.t: No: steering with it is the causal check
Yes: a high projection means the direction is driving it

predict.why: Projection is correlational. Adding the vector and watching behaviour change is what tests cause.

object.where: Any linear readout: probes, deception detectors, spam scores, one sheet across one arrow.
